title: The Same Boat
logline: A fisherman's boat has been repaired so many times that no original plank is left, but everyone still calls it by the same name.

object.note: Object 1 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The question left by the novices' memorised map, a name for everything inside, meets an outside mirror: a boat still called by one name though its planks have all been replaced.

thread_out.thread: From the salt water the boat works on to the fresh water a village waits for: after a thing that stays 'the same' while every part changes, a thing that is named though it is only empty space.

lesson.in_simple_terms: A boat can keep its name even when every plank has been replaced, because the name belongs to the way the parts are put together and to the shared story, not to any one piece of wood. Take the boat apart and you find planks, not 'a boat'.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: හැම ලෑල්ලක්ම මාරු කළත් ඔරුවට එකම නම පවතින්නේ, ඒ නම කිසියම් ලෑල්ලකට නොව කොටස් එකට සවි වී ඇති ආකාරයට අප දෙන සම්මුතියක් නිසාය.
lesson.the_teaching: The texts give a simple test: divide a thing, and if what first seemed present disappears, as cloth dissolves into threads, it is a concept (paññatti), not an ultimate reality. One text uses a table: no leg or board is the table, and apart from those pieces there is no table, so 'table' is a notion that arises from how the pieces are arranged; what remains at the end of dividing is what the texts call ultimate (paramattha). The same method is turned on a person, who is taken apart into five heaps (khandha), each a collection of many passing moments of one kind.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film watches old planks come out and new ones being shaped, the boat's name painted on again, and the fisherman remembering the boat's past, then follows its first launch after repair. Nobody on the beach doubts it is the same boat, and the viewer sees both at once: the name everyone shares, and the wood, tar and labour that are actually there.

key_terms.en: collective concept: a whole made of parts
ultimate reality, what remains under analysis

lesson.caution: This does not mean the boat is fake or that the fisherman is wrong to call it the same boat; everyday names are valid in their own domain, and the point is only that the name is not an extra thing hidden inside the wood.
lesson.builds_on: The novices learned a map for taking the mind apart; here the same method of taking apart is tried on something you can touch, a boat that stays 'the same' while its parts change.
